quarterly_data.signal: Omvoh (mirikizumab-mrkz) one-year post hoc composite-outcome analyses from the Phase 3 LUCENT and VIVID programs, to be presented at UEG Week 2026: in ulcerative colitis (LUCENT-2), 27.7% of Omvoh-treated patients achieved comprehensive disease control (simultaneous symptomatic, endoscopic and histologic remission, fecal calprotectin normalization and no corticosteroid use) versus 14% on placebo, and 23.4% versus 9.4% among patients with prior biologic failure (35.3% of the analysis); in Crohn's disease (VIVID-1), 20.4% achieved corticosteroid-free deep remission versus 2% on placebo, and 15.7% versus none among patients with prior biologic failure (48.6% of the analysis). Among Omvoh-treated patients, 91.1% of those achieving comprehensive disease control also achieved IBDQ remission (vs 65.2% of those who did not), and 88.1% of those achieving corticosteroid-free deep remission (vs 51%). Lilly says Omvoh is the first IL-23p19 inhibitor evaluated for comprehensive disease control in UC (company claim).
quarterly_data.figure: UC comprehensive disease control 27.7% vs 14% placebo (prior biologic failure 23.4% vs 9.4%); Crohn's corticosteroid-free deep remission 20.4% vs 2% (prior biologic failure 15.7% vs none)

quarterly_data.signal: Omvoh regulatory status and development program: Omvoh is approved for moderately to severely active UC and Crohn's disease in adults in 47 countries, and as a single-injection maintenance regimen for adults with UC in several countries including the U.S., EU, Canada and Japan. Lilly is pursuing mirikizumab combination studies in UC with eltrekibart (NCT06598943, an anti-neutrophil-inflammation monoclonal antibody) and zotemtegrast (NCT07186101, an oral alpha4beta7 integrin inhibitor), and in Crohn's disease with an FXR agonist (NCT07483099); the COMMIT-UC (NCT06937086) and COMMIT-CD (NCT06937099) trials study mirikizumab with an incretin-based therapy in adults with UC or Crohn's disease and obesity or overweight; pediatric trials, including a Phase 3 study in pediatric Crohn's disease (NCT05509777), are ongoing.
